## Why visit

The clearest reason for cider enthusiasts to give Chester serious space in the itinerary. CAMRA’s 2026 branch award describes more than a hundred real ciders and perries, and the bar’s own emphasis on different beer styles, lambic and mixed fermentation broadens the appeal to experienced European beer travellers. Ask for guidance by apple variety, maker, sweetness or fermentation character rather than simply ordering whichever cider is on draught. It is a modern specialist bar, so combine it with the Brewery Tap or Albion for historic surroundings. Flights and sharing bottles make a deliberate tasting visit particularly rewarding.

## Beer

Official site describes a broad draught and bottle range including dark and sour beer; CAMRA records cask introduced in 2024. Verify current cask availability.

**Recently seen or reported (not regulars):** Pomona Island — Tarquell.

*Recheck the dispense and beer clip at the bar. A handpump is not proof that a beer is cask-conditioned; similarly, these beer names do not establish real-cider qualification.*

## Cider and perry

**Real cider documented; reconfirm stock.** CAMRA National Cider/Perry Pub of the Year 2024 and West Cheshire winner 2026; extensive real-cider/perry bottle range plus changing draught. Also a 2026 national finalist (overall winner elsewhere).

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Plan the visit

Use the Foregate Street venue, not its old Chester Market address. Monthly clubs and tastings need date/booking confirmation.

**Getting there:** On Foregate Street between the station approach and the historic centre.
